classificationPolicy.Confirmed: The finding's bounded factual claim is supported by direct evidence and either an agreeing audit or source/existing-data corroboration. Caveats remain binding.
classificationPolicy.False Positive: The finding's headline or causal conclusion is contradicted or materially overbroad; a narrower metric may still be valid.
classificationPolicy.Needs Evidence: The direction may be plausible, but a material quantifier, causal attribution, semantic judgment, or population definition is not closed by the available evidence.

sharedEvidence: Both audits read the same production deployment and substantially overlapping 2026-09-15 window.
Both audits used the same pg_stat_statements reset window and the same underlying corpus tables, so near-identical database totals are agreement, not independent replication.
Both audits inspected the same repository base commit 8e4f4fc; matching source citations are not two independent code observations.
independentCorroboration: FABLE and OPUS ran different package-page HTTP samples; both found approximately 95% 503 responses outside the excluded 502 deploy window.
OPUS measured live CPU steal without Lightsail API access, independently corroborating FABLE's Lightsail-credit and host-pressure evidence but not independently proving credit exhaustion.

Current-worktree read-only source inspection confirmed pool defaults, fail-closed page paths, unbounded cluster loading, receipt-status rule divergence, unguarded snapshot upserts, expression indexes, safe-log omission, the stale schema text, and duplicate 0034 migration numbers.
Read-only recomputation over the frozen JSON candidate arrays produced the package rankings included below; it does not turn the underlying production export into independent evidence.
evidenceIndependence.reasonNoNewProductionProbes: The frozen audits already showed a starved host and high refusal rate. Additional traffic or database work would add load without resolving the semantic and longitudinal evidence gaps.

auditFindings.basis: FABLE directly read Lightsail credits; OPUS independently measured sustained steal, zero idle and no cgroup throttle.
caveats: Burst-credit exhaustion itself was not independently corroborated by OPUS.

auditFindings.basis: Independent HTTP samples found 28/29 and 47/50 package-page 503s, and source confirms two interactive connections, a 250 ms deployed wait, and fail-closed required reads.
caveats: The rate is a time-window estimate, not a permanent population parameter.

auditFindings.basis: The 5-minute interval overrun and write amplification are confirmed, but OPUS observed one completed 8m36s pass and another exceeding 20 minutes rather than a completed 40-minute pass.
caveats: Treat 8m36s to more than 20 minutes as the independently bounded observation; do not call 40 minutes a typical pass duration yet.

auditFindings.basis: Both exports identify the same query family at about 337k calls, 95.6k seconds and 82.5k seconds of block-read time; source confirms ecosystem filtering and the 500-row cap happen after the unbounded read.
The audits agree on all three query variants and source contains the MATERIALIZED authoring coverage family plus long statement ceilings.
caveats: Attribution to a specific poll route is strongest for the server-log window, not for every historical pg_stat_statements call.

auditFindings.basis: FABLE captured an EXPLAIN over all 109,701 edges and the current source retains the whole-table grouping shape.
caveats: No second audit repeated this EXPLAIN; current latency is amplified by host starvation.

auditFindings.basis: 502 storms and pre-listen reconciliation are directly evidenced, but OPUS excluded the same 502s as deploy-window artifacts and page views are not logged.
caveats: The absolute statements every restart and everyone are not measured; a controlled deploy timeline with page-route logging is required.

auditFindings.basis: Both safe-log analyses show the shard route returning 429s, including 749 on the audit date and 1,354 the prior day.
caveats: Client retry/backoff behavior remains unverified.

auditFindings.basis: FABLE's exhaustive latest-receipt export contains 120 FAIL and 97 SKIPPED live samples; OPUS independently found 166 live samples with a FAIL beside a PASS and source confirms any-pass badge behavior.
caveats: Environment changes explain part of the set; intended verification environments are absent for 215/217.

auditFindings.basis: The audits agree on 518 identical-contract groups, 677 redundant samples and 44 shared-case groups.
caveats: FABLE's purl+symbols duplicate count is a near-coordinate definition, not OPUS's stricter contract-identical exact definition.

auditFindings.basis: The exhaustive candidate export supports the spelling counts and current source contains multiple normalization branches and comments documenting the two spellings.
caveats: The raw-at candidate list has 54 rows while the aggregate says 68 manifests; the aggregate is retained, but the candidate-list coverage is incomplete.

auditFindings.basis: The exhaustive receipt aggregation directly supports 1,679 live samples without a PASS receipt naming an image digest.
caveats: This is missing provenance, not proof the runs used mutable images.

auditFindings.basis: Both audits compute 5,713 of 6,621 CROSS_PASS samples with fewer than two PASS peer keys and five PASS-signing keys corpus-wide.
caveats: The count proves the persisted receipt gap, not that the author and verifier were actually the same actor.

auditFindings.basis: No-subject, no-symbol and manifest/case mismatch counts agree exactly, but template-goal counts use different regexes and symbol-support heuristics range from a 105 floor through 157 to 798 samples.
caveats: Publish the predicates with every count; semantic symbol correctness needs parsing or re-execution.

auditFindings.basis: The frozen export finds 388 coordinates a major behind the newest observed version, while OPUS's recency test finds almost no versions unseen for 30 days and explicitly rejects staleness as the primary problem.
caveats: Newest observed is not necessarily latest stable or demanded; registry and demand validation are required before calling these defects.

auditFindings.basis: Wanted-board package/version coverage is correctly high, but the headline inference that demand is already saturated is contradicted by FABLE's own 1,775 observed packages without samples and OPUS's 14.5% uncovered project-bucket demand.
caveats: Retain the narrower facts: 1,180/1,192 wanted packages and 4,578/4,627 wanted versions are covered.

auditFindings.basis: Source inspection confirms page routes are skipped and duration is deleted from the safe access log.
caveats: Live curl and Playwright can measure point samples; the finding is about retained server-side history.

auditFindings.basis: Both audits report matching churn, size, memory and near-unused-index totals, and source confirms unconditional snapshot updates.
caveats: Lifetime counters lack a table-stat reset timestamp and must not be presented as a recent rate.

auditFindings.basis: FABLE's authenticated probe and both log analyses confirm farm-aggregate timeouts and dropped analytics writes.
caveats: Browser-side admin rendering cost was not measured.

auditFindings.basis: Different package-page samples converge at roughly 95% 503, with source-confirmed pool and fail-closed mechanisms.
caveats: The Wilson interval applies only to OPUS's uniform 50-coordinate draw.

auditFindings.basis: The observed 8m36s pass exceeds the 5-minute interval, a following pass exceeded 20 minutes, and FABLE independently found the same interval overrun and write amplification.
caveats: Continuously owns the pool is an operational summary; per-connection occupancy for the entire window was not traced.

auditFindings.basis: Repeated vmstat samples, since-boot counters, cgroup inspection and FABLE's separate host/API observations agree on severe CPU starvation.
caveats: OPUS alone did not prove the Lightsail credit mechanism.

auditFindings.basis: The 5,713 receipt-rule failures, one-receipt population, second promotion path and public L4 badge are confirmed; unearned is stronger than the records prove because an author-side LOCAL_PASS may have occurred but was not persisted.
caveats: Confirmed conclusion: the label is not auditable from stored receipts and independence is unenforced in the cited promotion path. Actual non-independence requires session-to-peer evidence.

auditFindings.basis: Matching query totals and source-level unbounded read behavior corroborate the finding.
FABLE reports the same roughly 10.4M calls and 66k seconds; source confirms the multi-CTE SQL function sits in two expression indexes.
caveats: The attribution to index maintenance is strongly supported by the call pattern and source, but pg_stat_statements does not itself label the caller.

auditFindings.basis: Both audits report 2.33M unconditional snapshot upserts, 20.0M guarded cluster upserts and only 84,580 cluster row changes; source confirms both SQL forms.
Server-log cadence, query-family totals and FABLE's authenticated endpoint probe agree on the timeout condition.
caveats: Every poll refers to the measured observation window, not all historical polls.

auditFindings.basis: The literal claim that memory is why nothing stays cached is contradicted by OPUS's own 95.85% overall hit rate and at least 96% for tables outside evidence_agg and failure_clusters.
caveats: Retain the narrower confirmed finding: those two oversized hot tables have 64.38% and 76.15% hit rates and account for 94.6% of lifetime block reads; causal ranking against churn and CPU steal needs a controlled delta.

auditFindings.basis: Caddy source independently confirms web-page log omission and duration deletion; both audits found the same API error families.

The 9x weekly output decline, 1,775 observed packages without samples and 128,590 diagnostic candidates are direct counts, but untouched and the Farm-causality chain rely on point polls and an external incident narrative.
caveats: A time series of queue admissions, offers, claims and completions by lane is required.

auditFindings.basis: The project-bucket aggregation is internally complete and FABLE independently reports the same 1,775 evidence-observed packages without samples.
caveats: Project buckets are a demand proxy polluted by optional binaries; they are not users, searches or callable API demand.

auditFindings.basis: Both heuristics find unsupported declarations, but counts differ materially because FABLE searches full symbols while OPUS searches last segments and separately removes package-name symbols.
caveats: Use 105 as a conservative candidate floor, 157 as OPUS's working set, and do not merge either with FABLE's 798 without a common parser.

auditFindings.basis: Both audits confirm templated goals and exactly 1,809 missing subjects; 5,406 is the broad ^verify population and 3,506 is FABLE's narrower verify-in-pkg template.
caveats: The broad and narrow template counts answer different questions and must remain separately labeled.

auditFindings.basis: Identical-contract and shared-case totals match exactly, and both identify post-dedup accumulation.
caveats: Exact means packages+symbols+contract in OPUS; near means packages+symbols.

auditFindings.basis: The frozen exhaustive export supports the job/draft/table counts; current-source search independently confirms the six named tables have no repository definitions or references.
caveats: Receipts on quarantined samples are retained evidence, not necessarily garbage.

auditFindings.basis: Current source still contains the zero-modern-cluster statement and both 0034 migration files; production counts in the frozen export show 229,517 complete clusters.
caveats: Duplicate numbering is confusing but lexical migration order keeps it non-breaking today.

auditFindings.basis: Both audits report the 26 MB manifest trigram index and one lifetime scan.
caveats: Lifetime idx_scan is reset-sensitive; no reset timestamp was available for table/index counters.

auditFindings.basis: One 48.84s cold request, one 1.23s warm request and one post-restart cancellation are valid point observations, but they do not establish a stable every-window or every-restart cost.
caveats: Repeat bounded cold rebuilds after host stabilization and retain route duration before prioritizing a sitemap-specific fix.

undersampled.method: Observed distinct project buckets, zero live samples; platform-specific optional binaries excluded. This ranks evidence-backed opportunity, not guaranteed authorability.
caveats: Project buckets include resolved transitive packages.
generic/cli coordinates require a product-policy decision because the current web router does not serve generic package pages.
Wanted-only pub and Go standard-library coordinates have no comparable project-bucket value.

oversampled.method: Samples per observed project bucket, restricted by OPUS to packages with at least five samples; zero-observation packages sort first. Duplicate-contract ranking is shown separately because high absolute density on popular packages is not itself waste.
caveats: This is a prioritization ratio, not proof that any individual sample lacks unique semantic value.
FABLE's density table shows that pgx/v5, x/net and x/sys are high-density but also high-demand; they are not labeled oversampled solely by count.

remediationOrder.action: Stop the starvation loop before query tuning: move production off exhausted burst capacity or reduce builder duty cycle below available baseline, and set the interval no shorter than the measured completed pass.
After headroom exists, restore the interactive pool policy from the 2-connection/250ms override toward the shipped 6-connection/3s values, with refusal and latency monitoring.

Remove builder write amplification: no-op guard snapshots, skip unchanged clusters before SQL or compare digests, batch target evidence, and replace the purl expression-index function with a stored normalized coordinate.

Make trust output auditable: gate L4/CROSS_PASS presentation on persisted independent evidence, surface latest verification result, require failure details, and requeue the 217 latest non-PASS samples with explicit intended environments.
Bound package failure-cluster reads in SQL by ecosystem and page limit, avoid wide JSONB columns until requested, and add a covering/index-only serving path.
Materialize builder-fed authoring/farm and dependency summaries instead of re-running whole-corpus CTEs and whole-edge aggregates on polls and page views.
Add privacy-safe web route class, status and duration telemetry; preserve restart logs; then validate 502, sitemap, memory and page-latency hypotheses with short counter deltas.
Serve through deploy/restart reconciliation or keep the old container until the new one is listening and healthy; validate with logged page routes before calling the 502 issue closed.
Normalize purls at ingest and receipt/wanted linkage, enforce publish-time duplicate checks, and repair the incomplete raw-at candidate export.

Retarget corpus work using filtered project-bucket demand plus wanted asks: exclude optional binaries, prioritize the undersampled list, and suppress byte-identical contract re-publication across unchanged releases.
Add bounded retry/backoff validation for shard 429/502 responses and tune the limiter only after observing client behavior.

Clean documented hygiene after availability work: update schema text, resolve duplicate migration numbering prospectively, triage orphan drafts/tables, and review the near-unused trigram index with reset-aware counters.
